name: Historical-US-mean anchoring with source marginal shapes retained
interpretation: Exploratory transport scenario for later US adults aged 20+, not an identified estimate of the later surveillance distribution.

transformation.grid_weights: Equal weights, 1/n, for each marginal grid
transformation.rank_constraint: Preserve the supplied order separately within each biomarker; never infer pairings from common row positions.
retained_features: Each supplied marginal's relative quantile spacing and coefficient of variation
The supplied smaller-root lognormal shape for each biomarker, subject to finite-grid representation

tc_reference_mean_mg_dl.provenance: Carroll et al., JAMA 2012, Table 1, 2007–2010, age-standardized US adults aged 20+
tc_reference_mean_mg_dl.applicability: Used fully as an earlier-US reference mean because geography, adult age definition and age standard match the intended population more closely than Mwanza. Persistence into the later period is an explicit scenario assumption.

hdl_reference_mean_mg_dl.provenance: Carroll et al., JAMA 2012, Table 1, 2007–2010, age-standardized US adults aged 20+
hdl_reference_mean_mg_dl.applicability: Used fully as an earlier-US reference mean, with the same unverified temporal-transport assumption as TC.

age_standardization.implementation: Interpret the equal-weight output grids as reference-standardized marginal distributions. The reference means were standardized; no individual ages or age-specific distributions are available to perform or verify direct standardization of the output distributions.

source_shape_transfer.decision: Retain as a working assumption, not as validated US evidence
source_shape_transfer.rationale: No target dispersion or tail information is supplied. Keeping the existing shapes avoids inventing new dispersion coefficients, but does not establish that the source shapes describe US adults.
